title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals — One Open Appeal per Party per Determination
content:
**Rule.** Under **Unemployment Insurance Appeals**, a claimant or employer may have several appeals at once, against different determinations or on different dockets, so the number of appeals per customer is not capped. An appeal is accepted for filing only when the same party has no other appeal against the same determination or decision with status filed, scheduled or decided. A party's second letter about a determination already under appeal is added to the existing appeal file as argument, and another party's appeal of the same determination is a separate appeal heard together with the first.

## What the rule looks at

- **The object.** The test is drawn per pair of *party* and *appealed record*: the appellant, and the determination or decision the appeal names. Appeals of the same party against other records do not count, and neither do appeals of other parties against the same record.
- **The authority.** The test is decided on the Department's appeal records — the party's appeals naming the same determination or decision and the status each one stands at before the new filing is accepted — not on the party's own account of what it has filed.
- **The statuses that count.** Only an appeal standing at filed, scheduled or decided status counts. An earlier appeal of the same party against the same record that stands withdrawn, dismissed or closed is not counted by this rule.
- **No overall cap.** Apart from this test there is no limit on how many appeals one customer may hold.

## Condition, judgement and result

| Same party | Same determination or decision | That other appeal's status | Result under this rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | filed, scheduled or decided | not accepted as a new appeal; the party's letter is added to the existing appeal file as argument |
| yes | yes | withdrawn, dismissed or closed | not counted by this rule |
| yes | no (a different record) | any | not counted by this rule; several appeals at once are allowed |
| no (another party) | yes | any | a separate appeal, heard together with the first |

## Illustrations (hypothetical parties)

- A claimant appeals a separation determination and, while that appeal stands scheduled, writes again about the same determination. The second letter is not a second appeal: it joins the first appeal's file as argument.
- The same claimant also appeals a different determination — an overpayment determination. Different record, so the two appeals stand side by side.
- The separating employer appeals the same separation determination the claimant appealed. That is another party's appeal: it is a separate appeal and is heard together with the claimant's.
